A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the tumor suppressor Dab2ip is a target of miR-149, and that the miRNA is able to downregulate DAB2IP both in cancer cells and in endothelial cells, contributing to the promotion of cancer progression.
miR- 149-3p, by targeting the tumor suppressor Dab2ip, promotes cancer progression through a dual mechanism, by enhancing aggressiveness of tumor cells and by remodeling the tumor micro-environment.

The main takeaway from our work is that
DAB2IP can be inactivated in cancer cells by multiple molecular mechanisms.
the DAB2IP-miR-149 axis represents an attractive therapeutic target for cancer treatment.
the miRNA-mediated regulation of DAB2ip can be a critical determinant of cancer aggressiveness and metastatic potential.
